newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy and France push for EU Middle East role.
newsitem.headline: Italy and France push for EU Middle East role.

text.p: Italy and France launched a joint push for a bigger European role in the faltering Middle East peace process on Friday before holding separate meetings with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat.

French President Jacques Chirac and Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi told a news conference in Naples after a morning of talks that they hoped a European Union summit in Dublin on Saturday would make clear Europe's desire to spur peace efforts.
Chirac said Paris and Rome would ask their partners to issue a statement stressing the EU's will to revive the peace process, threatened by five days of Israeli-Palestinian clashes last week.
"I believe everyone will agree to it," Chirac said.
Italy and France, irked at being left out of a peace process launched in Europe in 1991 but now increasingly led by the United States, have long lobbied for a stronger role.
Arafat flew to Naples to brief Prodi on this week's inconclusive Middle East summit in Washington, to which Europeans were not invited, and was to meet Chirac in Paris later in the day.

Deputy Prime Minister Walter Veltroni, who attended the Naples talks along with Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini, quoted Arafat as saying he was "very worried" after the Washington meeting, which Palestinian officials have deemed a failure.

It was Arafat's first chance to brief Europeans on the summit, called by President Bill Clinton in response to clashes in which 73 people died after Israel opened a tunnel in Jerusalem near Arab holy sites.
Dini told reporters the results of the Washington meeting "should be considered disappointing".
"There is no alternative to the peace process and there is no alternative to implementing the accords (between Israel and the Palestinians) which have already been signed," he said.

One Italian diplomat said: "This is a strong message and it's the one Dini will take to Dublin tomorrow and which Italy hopes will emerge from Europe alongside an expression of its desire for an active role."
Israel's new right-wing government has refused to set a date for an agreed final troop pull-out from the West Bank town of Hebron, the only site it has yet to hand over to Palestinian self-rule.
The leaders of the 15 EU states will meet in Dublin on Saturday for a special one-day summit to try to speed up progress on a revision of the EU's workings and treaties.
Chirac said Europe was a major financial aid donor in the Middle East and was eager not to let "intolerance and hate" gain the upper hand in the region.
Dini said it was important "that the heads of state and government...give a sense of direction and (express) the way they think this process should go".
Last week's clashes in Jerusalem, the Gaza Strip and the West Bank prompted Clinton to summon the leaders of Israel, the Palestinian Authority and Jordan to Washington.
Israel and the Palestinians are due to hold further talks on Sunday at the Erez crossing between Palestinian-ruled Gaza and Israel for a U.S.-brokered meeting.
